svg.text: Each RTL8221B gets its own 0.95 V buck. POW_EXT_SWR (pin 46) enables that buck after 3.3 V is up.
Datasheet: 0.95 V typical 364 mA, max 650 mA. One TPS54302 per PHY stays inside the 3 A limit.
DDR3 1.5 V is a separate TPS54302. VTT is TPS51200 with functional pins. Confirm the DSK-10 numbers in SLUS804.
V095_SOC is a ninth buck. 6.04k/10.2k targets 0.95 V. Change the divider if the Realtek core voltage differs.
PHY1 0.95 V EN = EN_095_P1 from POW_EXT_SWR
PHY2 0.95 V EN = EN_095_P2 from POW_EXT_SWR
PHY3 0.95 V EN = EN_095_P3 from POW_EXT_SWR
PHY4 0.95 V EN = EN_095_P4 from POW_EXT_SWR
PHY5 0.95 V EN = EN_095_P5 from POW_EXT_SWR
PHY6 0.95 V EN = EN_095_P6 from POW_EXT_SWR
PHY7 0.95 V EN = EN_095_P7 from POW_EXT_SWR
PHY8 0.95 V EN = EN_095_P8 from POW_EXT_SWR
DDR3 rail, termination, and the switch-core placeholder
DDR VDD/VDDQ 1.50 V. EN tied to V5. 15.4k/10.2k -> 1.496 V.
SoC core placeholder. Confirm the voltage in the Realtek hardware design guide.
EN is tied to V5. Resequence this enable if the HDG requires it. Resize FB for the real core voltage.
DDR VREF and TPS51200. Pin numbers on U_TPS51200 are functional, not the DSK-10 ball map.
MT41K256M16 power pins are on sheet 10. Address and DQ balls follow the Realtek DDR3 pin table.
